title: Dissociation and reaggregation of Hydra vulgaris for studies of self-organization
protocol: Collect 50–70 non-budding Hydra.
Thoroughly wash collected Hydra in Hydra media.
Wash Hydra again in ice-cold ddH2O.
Resuspend Hydra in ice-cold dissociation medium using an unpolished Pasteur pipette.
Incubate resuspended Hydra at 4°C.
Pause the experiment if Hydra have not been fed within the last 24 hours and allow them to remain in their new dish for another 24 hours before proceeding.
Wash Hydra 5 times with 21°C–25°C Hydra media.
Remove approximately 75%–90% of the original Hydra media using a clean 15 cm Pasteur pipette.
Aggressively spray Hydra feet attached to the near-empty dish with a Hydra media squirt bottle, aiming to detach as many Hydra from the surface as possible.
Angle and stabilize the stream of the bottle to form a whirlpool in the well of the dish to collect the Hydra in the middle for easier media removal.
Collect and dispose of floating debris while the Hydra are grouped in the middle of the dish after forming the whirlpool.
Scrape the plastic bottom of culture dishes during Hydra transfer using a Pasteur pipette.
Repeat the process four times until Hydra are thoroughly cleaned and debris is removed.
Wash Hydra four times with 0°C ddH2O.
Cool ddH2O rapidly in a glass 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Thaw dissociation media in a 500 mL graduated cylinder filled with warm water or prepare fresh from concentrated stock solutions.
Vortex thawed tubes to re-dissolve any precipitate as needed.
Place the media on ice to bring it to 0°C.
Wash Hydra using a glass Pasteur pipette to agitate and create a whirlpool in the dish, collecting Hydra in the center.
Remove media after each wash to ensure debris is removed.
Terminate the experiment if large chunks or wisps of Hydra tissue appear in the media.
Terminate the experiment if the media clouds, indicating premature disintegration and osmotic shock-induced damage to cells.
Incubate Hydra in dissociation media at 4°C.
Whirlpool Hydra gently with a Pasteur pipette to collect them in the center of the dish.
Transfer collected Hydra to a pre-chilled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, minimizing ddH2O carryover.
Let Hydra sediment to the bottom of the tube.
Remove as much media as possible from the tube.
Using a Pasteur pipette, bring the volume of the tube to 1.5 mL with ice-cold dissociation media.
Allow Hydra to settle before removing as much media as possible.
Again bring the volume of the tube to approximately 1.5 mL with ice-cold dissociation media.
Aspirate the Hydra approximately 10 times into and from the pipette.
Incubate Hydra.
Triturate Hydra with approximately 20 plunges until the media begins to cloud, indicating the start of dissociation.
Replace dissociation media and triturate Hydra with 60 plunges until the media becomes opaque.
Allow tissue chunks to sediment on ice for 1 minute.
Remove as much media and debris as possible without disturbing the Hydra.
Resuspend Hydra in roughly 1.3–1.5 mL of fresh, ice-cold dissociation media.
Invert the closed tube several times to resuspend and redistribute the Hydra.
Place the tube on its side in a 4°C refrigerator.
Replace dissociation media every half hour for a total of three times over a 2-hour incubation period.
Aspirate the Hydra gently around 10 times before allowing the animals to sediment after each media replacement.
Remove as much media as possible, add fresh media to 1.3–1.5 mL, and redistribute the Hydra by inverting the closed tube.
Decant ice-cold ddH2O from the flask containing Hydra.
Vortex Hydra toward the center of the plate using a pipette, working rapidly and constantly.
Remove approximately 75% of the ddH2O and repeat the process two more times.
Vortex Hydra during the fourth wash and transfer them to a pre-chilled microcentrifuge tube with minimal carryover of ddH2O.
Add ice-cold dissociation media to the microcentrifuge tube to reach a total volume of 1.5 ml.
Remove as much of this initial media and replace it with fresh dissociation media.
Triturate Hydra ten times in the new media.
Replace the dissociation media again after trituration.
Incubate the Hydra at 4°C for approximately one hour.
Exchange the dissociation media a final time after pre-dissociation.
Compress the bulb.
Angle the tip of an unpolished, fresh Pasteur pipette toward the bottom of the microcentrifuge tube containing the Hydra.
Rest the side of the pipette against the lip of the tube opening.
Place the bore of the pipette as close to the bottom as possible without creating a seal.
Draw approximately 90% of the contents of the tube into the pipette.
Expel the contents while maintaining the same angle of the pipette tip.
Avoid emptying the entire volume to prevent the production of bubbles.
Repeat this process 10–20 times, maintaining the angle of the pipette and avoiding the generation of bubbles with the pipette.
Plunge the pipette at a rate of approximately one complete cycle per second.
Allow the animals to sediment after each plunging cycle.
Replace the cloudy dissociation media with fresh dissociation media before proceeding with the actual dissociation.
Dissociate the Hydra into individual cells.
Expel air from the plunger and insert the pipette into the tube in the described position.
Draw approximately 90% of the contents into the pipette and expel, avoiding bubbles.
Repeat the process 50-100 times until the media is nearly opaque.
Perform the dissociation next to a bright background for easier observation.
Sediment tissue fragments on ice.
Collect the cell supernatant.
Place the tube containing dissociated Hydra on ice for 1 minute.
Check the final volume of undissociated tissue fragments.
Rinse the pipette tip to remove residual adherent tissue fragments.
Carefully collect the cell-containing supernatant without disturbing the tissue sediment.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Gently resuspend the cell suspension in a 1.5 mL tube with a Pasteur pipette.
Add one drop of cell suspension to each side of the hemocytometer.
Count the cells to determine the concentration.
Note any clumps of cells, if present.
Allocate cells for aggregates of desired size to pre-chilled 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes at a final volume of 200 μL.
Sediment the allocated cells on ice for 30 min.
Determine the volume to add to achieve aggregates of the sizes required for the experiment.
Determine the volume of ice-cold dissociation media needed to yield a final volume of 200 μL when added to the cell suspension.
Add the calculated volume of dissociation media to pre-chilled 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Gently add the cell suspension to the bottom of the tube containing the dissociation media.
Allow cells to sediment on ice for 30 min.
Sediment the cell suspension on ice for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension slowly for 4 minutes at 300 g.
Transfer the tubes to the centrifuge carefully without disturbing the sedimentation.
Centrifuge without a lid, if possible, to avoid disrupting the cell pellets.
Store the tubes in their rack at 4°C for 2–6 hours to allow reaggregation.
Inspect microcentrifuge tubes for cell pellets to ensure sedimentation and aggregation.
Mix cells in suspension for 30 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 4 minutes in a fixed-angle rotor.
Add ice to the bottom of an empty 1 mL pipette tip box serving as a 0.5 mL tube holder to slow temperature transition to 4°C and eventually to 18°C if desired.
Incubate aggregates at 4°C to facilitate detachment from the tube.
Transfer aggregates to pre-chilled 24-well plates after 4°C incubation.
Pre-chill the 24-well plate on ice and add 600 μL ice-cold dissociation medium.
Gently bounce the bottoms of the tubes in a 1 mL tip holder/tube rack to facilitate detachment.
Transfer 200 μL contents from a 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube to 600 μL dissociation medium in a well of a 24-well plate.
Inspect the Pasteur pipette to ensure aggregates are pulled from the bottom before the tube is empty.
Place the 24-well plate in an 18°C incubator.
Gradually dilute dissociation media back to normal Hydra media supplemented with Penicillin/Streptomycin at 6 h, 22 h, 46 h, and 70 h post-sedimentation.
For the first 50% dilution at 8 h, gently add another 800 μL of Hydra media to the 800 μL dissociation media in the well.
Subsequent dilutions should include removal of 800 μL of media before replacement.
